title: “Ultrasound-Assisted High-Fluidics Phacoaspiration”: An Efficient and Safe Technique for Nucleus Quadrant Workup Through 2.2 mm Mini- and 1.6 mm Micro-Incisions Following Manual or Femtosecond Laser Sectorial Lens Fragmentation
indication: Bilateral age-related cataract, immediate sequential bilateral cataract surgery; prospective randomized intraindividual comparison (one eye per arm) of high-fluidics coaxial phaco with the easyTip 2.2 through a 2.2 mm posterolimbal incision versus infusion-assisted easyTip COMICS through a 1.6 mm incision (Oertli OS3, direct-crack divide and conquer), one surgeon; excluded prior intraocular surgery, glaucoma, inflammatory eye disease, corneal disease

groups.description: High-fluidics phaco with easyTip 2.2 mini-needle through a 2.2 mm incision (eT2.2 HF)
High-fluidics infusion-assisted phaco with easyTip COMICS micro-needle through a 1.6 mm incision plus sideport infusion (eT1.6 iaCOMICS HF), fellow eye

series.baseline_label: Preoperative endothelial cell count measured 1 week before surgery (Methods)
series.notes: Table 3 'Endothelial Cell Count (ECC)' rows preop and 6 months postop, eT2.2 HF column; data are means ± SD when normally distributed (Statistics); n = 50 completers of the 6-month follow-up (table gives no n)

exclusions.reason: historical groups from earlier publications without ECD in this article

notes: 77 patients were randomized (one eye to each arm) and 50 completed the 6-month follow-up; Table 3 does not state whether the preoperative means include all 77 or only the 50 completers, so series n is the 50 completers.

Both arms are variants of the article's high-fluidics technique compared intraindividually and neither is declared experimental relative to the other; both recorded as control. The article contrasts them with previously published lower-fluidics results, which are not part of this record.
Both eyes of each patient were operated (immediate sequential bilateral surgery); the fellow eye is an operated arm, not an unoperated control.
